66209-to-sup-with-the-devil.title: To Sup With The Devil
66209-to-sup-with-the-devil.creator: Unknown
66209-to-sup-with-the-devil.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "No, not at all." George gulped down the last of his wine. "Quite pleasant if I may say so. Quite a change from the market and speculation and," he snorted loudly, "those damn commodities that I lost so heavily on yesterday. No, I think I'd enjoy seeing things as a demon or a ghoul or something."

arxiv-2303-01580.title: Mixture of Soft Prompts for Controllable Data Generation
arxiv-2303-01580.creator: Derek Chen Celine Lee Yunan Lu Domenic Rosati Zhou Yu
arxiv-2303-01580.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) effectively generate fluent text when the target output follows natural language patterns. However, structured prediction tasks confine the output format to a limited ontology, causing even very large models to struggle since they were never trained with such restrictions in mind.

arxiv-2310-04110.title: Automated 3D Segmentation of Kidneys and Tumors in MICCAI KiTS 2023 Challenge
arxiv-2310-04110.creator: Andriy Myronenko, Dong Yang, Yufan He, Daguang Xu
arxiv-2310-04110.description: Abstract Kidney and Kidney Tumor Segmentation Challenge (KiTS) 2023 [ 6 ] offers a platform for researchers to compare their solutions to segmentation from 3D CT. In this work, we describe our submission to the challenge using automated segmentation of Auto3DSeg 1 1 1 https://monai.io/apps/auto3dseg available in MONAI 2 2 2 https://github.com/Project-MONAI/MONAI .

arxiv-2407-13067.title: Large Language Model Agents for Improving Engagement with Behavior Change Interventions: Application to Digital Mindfulness
arxiv-2407-13067.creator: Harsh Kumar, Suhyeon Yoo, Angela Zavaleta Bernuy, Jiakai Shi, Huayin Luo, Joseph Williams, Anastasia Kuzminykh, Ashton Anderson, Rachel Kornfield
arxiv-2407-13067.description: Abstract . Although engagement in self-directed wellness exercises typically declines over time, integrating social support such as coaching can sustain it. However, traditional forms of support are often inaccessible due to the high costs and complex coordination. Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in providing human-like dialogues that could emulate social support.

arxiv-2503-00332.title: Investigating the use of terrain-following coordinates in AI-driven precipitation forecasts Thanks: Citation : Sha, Y. et al. Investigating the contribution of terrain-following coordinates and conservation schemes in AI-driven precipitation forecasts. Submitted for publication in Geophysical Resear
arxiv-2503-00332.creator: Yingkai Sha †, John S. Schreck †, William Chapman ‡, David John Gagne II †
arxiv-2503-00332.description: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) weather prediction (AIWP) models often produce “blurry” precipitation forecasts. This study presents a novel solution to tackle this problem—integrating terrain-following coordinates into AIWP models. Forecast experiments are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of terrain-following coordinates using FuXi, an example AIWP model, adapted to 1.0 ∘ grid spacing data.

arxiv-2504-05426.title: Survey on algorithms for multi-index models
arxiv-2504-05426.creator: Joan Bruna, Daniel Hsu
arxiv-2504-05426.description: Abstract We review the literature on algorithms for estimating the index space in a multi-index model. The primary focus is on computationally efficient (polynomial-time) algorithms in Gaussian space, the assumptions under which consistency is guaranteed by these methods, and their sample complexity.

arxiv-2510-00512.title: Adaptive Data-Knowledge Alignment in Genetic Perturbation Prediction
arxiv-2510-00512.creator: Yuanfang Xiang, Lun Ai
arxiv-2510-00512.description: Abstract The transcriptional response to genetic perturbation reveals fundamental insights into complex cellular systems. While current approaches have made progress in predicting genetic perturbation responses, they provide limited biological understanding and cannot systematically refine existing knowledge. Overcoming these limitations requires an end-to-end integration of data-driven learning and existing knowledge.

arxiv-2510-07474.title: Surrogate Modeling for the Design of Optimal Lattice Structures using Tensor Completion
arxiv-2510-07474.creator: Shaan Pakala University of California, Riverside spaka002@ucr.edu & Aldair E. Gongora Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory gongora1@llnl.gov Brian Giera Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory giera1@llnl.gov & Evangelos E. Papalexakis University of California, Riverside epapalex@cs.ucr.edu
arxiv-2510-07474.description: Abstract When designing new materials, it is often necessary to design a material with specific desired properties. Unfortunately, as new design variables are added, the search space grows exponentially, which makes synthesizing and validating the properties of each material very impractical and time-consuming. In this work, we focus on the design of optimal lattice structures with regard to mechanical performance.

arxiv-2510-13149.title: RoboHiMan: A Hierarchical Evaluation Paradigm for Compositional Generalization in Long-Horizon Manipulation
arxiv-2510-13149.creator: Yangtao Chen, Zixuan Chen, Nga Teng Chan, Junting Chen, Junhui Yin, Jieqi Shi, Yang Gao, Yong-Lu Li, Jing Huo
arxiv-2510-13149.description: Abstract Enabling robots to flexibly schedule and compose learned skills for novel long-horizon manipulation under diverse perturbations remains a core challenge. Early explorations with end-to-end VLA models show limited success, as these models struggle to generalize beyond the training distribution.

arxiv-2510-17934.title: AtlasKV: Augmenting LLMs with Billion-Scale Knowledge Graphs in 20GB VRAM
arxiv-2510-17934.creator: Haoyu Huang, Hong Ting Tsang, Jiaxin Bai, Xi Peng, Gong Zhang, Yangqiu Song
arxiv-2510-17934.description: Abstract Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has shown some success in augmenting large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge. However, as a non-parametric knowledge integration paradigm for LLMs, RAG methods heavily rely on external retrieval modules and the retrieved textual context prior.

arxiv-2511-05965.title: Adaptive Agent Selection and Interaction Network for Image-to-point cloud Registration
arxiv-2511-05965.creator: Zhixin Cheng, Xiaotian Yin, Jiacheng Deng, Bohao Liao, Yujia Chen, Xu Zhou, Baoqun Yin, Tianzhu Zhang
arxiv-2511-05965.description: Abstract Typical detection-free methods for image-to-point cloud registration leverage transformer-based architectures to aggregate cross-modal features and establish correspondences. However, they often struggle under challenging conditions, where noise disrupts similarity computation and leads to incorrect correspondences. Moreover, without dedicated designs, it remains difficult to effectively select informative and correlated representations across modalities, thereby limiting the robustness and accuracy of registration.

arxiv-2601-20065.title: Exploring the properties of the Hadronic Phase in Heavy-Ion Collisions at RHIC Energies via Partial Chemical Equilibrium
arxiv-2601-20065.creator: Rishabh Sharma, Chitrasen Jena, Volodymyr Vovchenko
arxiv-2601-20065.description: Abstract The hadronic phase in heavy-ion collisions plays a crucial role in shaping the final-state hadron abundances. In this work, we study Au+Au collisions at s NN = 7.7 \sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=7.7 – 200 200 GeV using the Hadron Resonance Gas model in Partial Chemical Equilibrium (HRG-PCE).

arxiv-2603-27866.title: Wan-R1: Verifiable-Reinforcement Learning for Video Reasoning
arxiv-2603-27866.creator: Ming Liu, Yunbei Zhang, Shilong Liu, Liwen Wang, Wensheng Zhang

plos-pone-0353348.title: A hybrid deep learning model for user story effort estimation
plos-pone-0353348.creator: Saadia Malik, Muhammad Hamid, Muhammad Saleem
plos-pone-0353348.description: A hybrid deep learning model for user story effort estimation

pmc-10600332.title: Hypochlorous acid in a double formulation (liquid plus gel) is a key prognostic factor for healing and absence of infection in chronic ulcers. A nonrandomized concurrent treatment study
pmc-10600332.creator: Rafael Herruzo, Erika Fondo Alvarez, Irene Herruzo, Macarena Garrido‐Estepa, Emma Santiso Casanova, Silvia Cerame Perez
pmc-10600332.description: Background and AimsDiverse protocols prevent infection and/or improve ulcer epithelialization. The existing protocols tend to antagonize the risk factors that promote the chronicity of this type of wound. Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is used to treat ulcers and wounds because of its antiseptic and noncytotoxic properties.

pmc-11599433.title: Advancing fracture management: the role of minimally invasive osteosynthesis in orthopedic trauma care
pmc-11599433.creator: Florian Wichlas, Gerwin Haybäck, Valeska Hofmann, Amelie Deluca, Andreas Traweger, Christian Deininger
pmc-11599433.description: PurposeMinimally Invasive Osteosynthesis (MIO) developed to be a key technique in orthopedic trauma surgery, offering a less invasive alternative for managing fractures in various anatomical regions. However, standardized guidelines for its application are lacking. This study aims to establish comprehensive principles for MIO to guide surgeons in treating different types of fractures and its locations.

pmc-11618040.title: Synthesis, Reactivity, and Bonding Analysis of a Tetracoordinated Nickel Carbene
pmc-11618040.creator: Pablo M Pérez‐García, María L G Sansores‐Paredes, Célia Fonseca Guerra, Pascal Vermeeren, Marc‐Etienne Moret
pmc-11618040.description: Nickel carbenes are key reactive intermediates in the catalytic cyclopropanation of olefins and other reactions, but isolated examples are scarce and generally rely on low coordination numbers (≤3) to stabilize the metal−ligand multiple bond. Here we report the isolation and characterization of a stable tetracoordinated nickel carbene bearing a triphosphine pincer ligand.

pmc-12500388.title: Automated Manufacturing of Carbon‐11 Radiopharmaceuticals Using Cassette‐Based Radiosynthesizers
pmc-12500388.creator: Michael L. Schulte, Adam J. Rosenberg
pmc-12500388.description: As the field of radiochemistry moves toward the rapid development and translation of radiopharmaceuticals, the radiosynthetic methodology and manufacturing are becoming more and more refined. As the use of radiopharmaceuticals in clinical research is one of the primary goals of radiochemistry research, compliance with cGMP regulations is a key factor in radiosynthesis developments.

pmc-12710031.title: Precise Image Color Correction Based on Dual Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Cooperative Flight
pmc-12710031.creator: Xuqi Lu, Jiayang Xie, Jiayou Yan, Ji Zhou, Haiyan Cen
pmc-12710031.description: Color accuracy and consistency in remote sensing imagery are crucial for reliable plant health monitoring, precise growth stage identification, and stress detection. However, without effective color correction, variations in lighting and sensor sensitivity often cause color distortions between images, compromising data quality and analysis.

pmc-12935573.title: Learning From Our Failures: When Anterior Temporal Lobectomies Fail
pmc-12935573.creator: Lia Ernst, Kathryn A Davis, Michael D Staudt, Chris Tailby, Sisira Yadala, Chengyuan Wu
pmc-12935573.description: Anterior temporal lobectomy (ATL) remains the standard surgical treatment for drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy, yet 20% to 30% of patients experience persistent seizures and/or unfavorable neuropsychological outcomes. These results highlight that postoperative success is influenced not only by the technical execution of surgery but also by the accuracy with which epileptogenic networks are characterized.

pmc-13002487.title: Aortic Root Thrombosis With Multivessel Coronary Embolism Following Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
pmc-13002487.creator: Radhay Parikh, Chloe Kharsa, Rody G. Bou Chaaya, Gal Sella, Mangesh Kritya, Karl Abou Zeid, Mahwash Kassi, Neal Kleiman, Alpesh R. Shah
pmc-13002487.description: BackgroundAortic root thrombosis is uncommon but potentially catastrophic in patients supported with continuous-flow left ventricular assist devices (LVADs).Case SummaryWe describe a 28-year-old woman presenting with syncope 1 month after HeartMate 3 LVAD implantation. Electrocardiography demonstrated a myocardial infarction. Echocardiography revealed severe biventricular dysfunction, persistent aortic valve closure, and normal LVAD inflow velocities. The international normalized ratio was 1.4.

pmc-13292431.title: Thinking and feeling matter: a second-order meta-analysis of student characteristics across developmental domains and their effect on academic outcomes
pmc-13292431.creator: Cahit Erdem, Metin Kaya, Mustafa Polat, Eray Eğmir

pmc-13355929.title: Emergent Spinning and Orbital Motion in Clustered Wind‐Assisted Flyers
pmc-13355929.creator: Bingnan Zhou, Rahul Chand, Fahad Ahmed Korai, Jianfeng Yang, Valtteri Savonen, Fan Liu, Qi Yang, Hao Zeng
pmc-13355929.description: Nature offers a rich diversity of wind‐assisted flyers, ranging from snowflakes to dandelion seeds and fungal spores. Despite their differences in size, material, and aerodynamic regime, these systems share a common principle: when individual flyers aggregate into clusters, the resulting geometric asymmetry gives rise to emergent behaviors, e.g., spinning, orbital motion, and extended gliding.

pmc-13474738.title: Effects of high- versus moderate-intensity multimodal whole-body training to improve inspiratory muscle function in persons with chronic nonspecific low back pain
pmc-13474738.creator: Sim Klaps, Jonas Verbrugghe, Nina Goossens, Sofie Van Wesemael, Bjorn Van Eecke, Albère Köke, Jeanine Verbunt, Daniel Langer, Lotte Janssens, Annick Timmermans
pmc-13474738.description: BackgroundTo compare the effects of a multimodal whole-body high-intensity training (HIT) program versus a moderate-intensity training (MIT) program on inspiratory muscle function in persons with chronic nonspecific low back pain (CNSLBP), and to investigate whether changes in inspiratory muscle function relate to changes in disability, pain intensity, anxiety, depression, and exercise capacity.

pmc-13556485.title: 341. Preliminary investigation of peripheral immune markers and synaptic density in trauma-exposed youth seeking mental health treatment
pmc-13556485.creator: M Zilberman, E Vieira, C Cote, L Yu, J Truong, Y Nikolova, E Dickie, S Ameis, K Desmond, L Narciso, C Uribe, D Kahana, N Vasdev, D Felsky, B Goldstein, K Cleverley, D Courtney, L Hawke, N Kozloff, A Polillo, M Rotenberg, L Quilty, W Wang, G Foussias, A Voineskos, J Warsh, O Husain, I Boileau
pmc-13556485.description: BackgroundAnimal studies show that stress triggers immune dysregulation, leading to elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and microglial activation. This response is linked to excessive synaptic pruning and reduced synaptic density, potentially raising vulnerability to mental illness. In humans, childhood trauma has been linked with elevated levels of plasma peripheral pro-inflammatory cytokines.
